chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from several of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from several of our companions from Ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the boy is valid if he has reached the age of discernment, and so is his will and his gift, even if he has not undergone puberty.
ai.seo_question: Is a boy's divorce valid before puberty in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify the fiqh of the pre-pubescent boy (al-ṣabī), distinguishing between physical maturity (ihtilām) and mental discernment (‘aql). This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for validating the legal acts (fi‘l) of children who possess sufficient intellect, even if they have not yet experienced seminal emission, thereby aligning legal capacity with cognitive understanding rather than solely biological signs of puberty.
